@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+name: test envs
+
+on: [push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch]
+
+jobs:
+  predict:
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
+        env: [env.yaml, env_cuda.yaml]
+        exclude:
+          - os: macos-latest   # no CUDA on macOS
+            env: env_cuda.yaml
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
+    env:
+      # runners have no GPU; lets conda pick CUDA builds (empty = no CUDA)
+      CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA: ${{ matrix.env == 'env_cuda.yaml' && '12.6' || '' }}
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        shell: bash -el {0}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: conda-incubator/setup-miniconda@v3
+        with:
+          miniforge-version: latest
+          environment-file: ${{ matrix.env }}
+          activate-environment: test
+      - name: Get RepoRT HSM/Tanaka databases
+        run: |
+          git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/michaelwitting/RepoRT.git ../RepoRT
+          git -C ../RepoRT sparse-checkout set resources/hsm_database resources/tanaka_database
+      - name: Check CUDA build of torch
+        if: matrix.env == 'env_cuda.yaml'
+        run: python -c "import torch; assert torch.version.cuda, 'torch built without CUDA'; print(torch.version.cuda)"
+      # hosted runners have no GPU, so predictions run on CPU for both envs
+      - name: predict.py
+        run: |
+          python predict.py --model models/2-step0525.pt --repo_root_folder ../RepoRT \
+            --input_compounds test/test_input.tsv --input_metadata test/test_metadata.yaml --out out.tsv
+          head out.tsv

issues.title: Windows environment problem, workflows for env-testing
issues.body:
See #1, includes #2.

- fixes windows environment, also for GPU/Cuda version
- GitHub workflow for making sure the environments work
- reactivate docker test workflow

issues.title: Fix windows install issue
issues.body:
See #1 

I have only tested the fix on windows, by testing predict.py. So probably good to quickly test linux as well, before considering merging. 

Apparently including the pytorch channel gave some issues. Removing the torch channel solved the torch issue, but yaml was not installed correctly, switching to pyyaml solved this. 

I did not check the env_cuda.yaml, but I assume this has the same issue (and hopefully same solution).

Hope this helps!

issues.title: Environment fails on windows
issues.body:
Hi @f-kretschmer,

I worked with the package on linux before and it all worked great. 
However, now I tried installing it on Windows and there was an issue with importing torch. 

When installing using:
conda env create -n 2-step -f env.yaml
conda activate 2-step

The install works, but the code doesn't run, due to an issue with torch: OSError: [WinError 182] The operating system cannot run %1. Error loading "C:\Users\jonge094\AppData\Local\miniconda3\envs\rt_prediction\Lib\site-packages\torch\lib\fbgemm.dll" or one of its dependencies.

I was able to resolve it locally after some back and forth with claude. I will make a PR with the yaml file that worked for me on windows. I expcet it will work fine on linux as well, but I didn't test this on linux or mac. So probably good to test that before merging.
